name: NVIDIA Enterprise Marketplace / Partner Network (NPN) as an acquisition channel
region: Worldwide; directory filterable by country (the SuperPOD specialization view is location=US in NVIDIA's own example link)
notes: QUOTE-ONLY by construction. Recorded separately from nvidia-dgx-direct because this is the ROUTING artefact rather than the hardware: marketplace.nvidia.com is where an enterprise actually finds the specific reseller, integrator or CSP that will sell it to them, and NVIDIA links to it as the 'Find a Partner' destination from the DGX page. Partner categories listed are Cloud Service Providers and Partner Servers, plus specializations that map to real buying needs (SuperPOD deployment expertise, DGX-Ready Lifecycle Management, colocation). Two consequences for anyone sourcing hardware: (1) the transacting legal entity is the partner, so warranty, support SLA and liability sit with them, not NVIDIA; (2) the directory is the practical place to see how many resellers a given country actually has, which is a real constraint on regional tenders. No public price anywhere on the directory. EXPORT CONTROLLED (true). Regime: US BIS advanced-computing export controls (the Oct 2023 interim final rule, 88 FR 73458 - source sup-buy-bis-2023-advanced-computing-controls), which put datacenter accelerators under ECCN 3A090/4A090, added the advanced-computing Foreign Direct Product (FDP) rule, and extended Regional Stability (RS) controls to Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5. For items destined to Macau or Country Group D:5 the rule applies a PRESUMPTION OF DENIAL; other RS destinations get a presumption of approval. Practical effect: which accelerator you can legally be sold, and which SKU counts as compliant, is set by destination and end user - not by the channel.
